_comment: WRITE-PATH FAIL-LOUD invariant, feature 3/9 follow-up (owner-flagged 2026-08-12,
ex feature-28/seeder-contract audit) -- the CONTRACT-MAP Layer 2 ledger entry for
two invariants pinned by REAL, already-executing suites elsewhere:
1. facade-insert-fails-loud-on-constraint-violation -- Database.insert() must
THROW on a real driver failure (NOT NULL / UNIQUE violation), matching
update()/delete()/truncate()/execute()/fetch(), never resolve to a falsy
{success:false} result. Node's SQLiteAdapter.insert() single-row path was
the one write method that caught the driver error and returned it instead
of throwing -- update()/delete()/truncate() already ran their adapter
result through the assertWrote() fail-loud check; insert() did not.
Python/PHP/Ruby were ALREADY correct (measured, not fixed): Python's and
Ruby's insert() is a thin wrapper over execute(), which never catches;
PHP's Database::insert() already had the explicit
`if ($result === false) throw new DatabaseException(...)` check.
2. orm-save-returns-false-on-constraint-violation -- BaseModel/ORM.save()'s
documented contract (`this | false`, never raises) must be UNCHANGED by
the fix above. Characterised, not changed, in all four: Node's save()
insert path never calls Database.insert() at all (it builds its own SQL
and runs it through adapterExecute(), already fail-loud, already wrapped
in save()'s own try/catch) -- so the facade fix has NO ripple into save().
Python/PHP/Ruby's save() already wraps db.insert()/->insert() in a
try/except|catch|rescue that converts the raise into `false` -- also
unaffected, also already correct.
THE EXECUTABLE FIXTURE for invariant 1 is `write_path_contract.json`, shipped
identically in all four repos' own test dirs (NOT under this directory -- it
predates the CONTRACT-MAP/audit-contract-fixtures.py convention, and each
language's runner is a genuine fixture INTERPRETER that loads and executes it,
unlike the textual case-name matching this ledger's own checker performs).
Because the runner files interpolate `kase.name` at runtime rather than naming
cases literally in source, `suites` below points at the FIXTURE JSON itself
(where the case name is a literal string) rather than the .ts/.py/.php/.rb
runner -- the real proof of execution is the runner actually iterating and
running every case in that file (see plan/v3/write-path-contract-fixture-driven.md),
independently reverified 2026-08-12: 24-25 cases green in all four (SQLite),
including this new one, before this ledger entry was written.
Invariant 2 has no shared JSON fixture (BaseModel/ORM save() is exercised
through each language's own ORM object, not a generic op-dispatch table), so
`suites` points at the real ormBaseContract test/spec file in each language,
which is where `save_on_constraint_violation_returns_false` actually lives
and runs.
NO MOCKS: every case drives a real temp/in-memory SQLite file through the
public Database/ORM facade; a real UNIQUE (invariant 1: PRIMARY KEY collision;
invariant 2: a UNIQUE index added for the case) constraint violation is the
failure under test, not a simulated one. Mutation-proved 2026-08-12: reverting
the Database.insert() assertWrote() check turned invariant 1's Node case RED
with the exact 'the op did not throw' failure; dropping the UNIQUE constraint
the invariant-2 cases add turned all four RED with 'expected false, got <the
newly-saved row>'. Both restored green before this fixture was committed.
Env contract (identical to the write-path runner): TINA4_TEST_WRITE_PATH_URL /
_USERNAME / _PASSWORD select a live engine; unset falls back to a temp/
in-memory SQLite file, which is what proved both invariants here.
feature: 3/9 - write-path fail-loud gap (owner-flagged, ex feature-28 follow-up)

invariants.rule: Database.insert() on a real driver failure (NOT NULL / UNIQUE violation) THROWS, matching update()/delete()/truncate()/execute()/fetch() -- never a falsy or {success:false} result. Identical in all four; Node was the only gap (fixed here), Python/PHP/Ruby were already correct.
invariants.why: A caller that does not inspect insert()'s return value silently believed the write landed. update()/delete()/truncate() already close this gap via the shared assertWrote() check (or PHP's equivalent explicit throw); insert() was the one write method that did not -- and only on Node's synchronous SQLite path (the async adapters -- Postgres/MySQL/MSSQL/Firebird -- already throw directly from their *Async methods, and adapterInsert(), the seeder's own internal helper added in feature 28, already carried this exact check with a comment naming the gap it was closing for seedTable()/seedOrm() specifically -- Database.insert() itself was the piece left over).

invariants.rule: BaseModel/ORM.save() keeps its documented `this | false` contract (never raises) on a real constraint violation, and writes nothing -- unaffected by the facade fix above, in all four, verified not changed.
invariants.why: The facade fix makes Database.insert() throw where it used to return a falsy result on SQLite. save()'s own insert path had to be characterised BEFORE the fix landed to rule out a ripple: in Node save() never calls Database.insert() (it builds its own SQL and runs it through the already-fail-loud adapterExecute(), already wrapped in save()'s own try/catch); in Python/PHP/Ruby save() already wraps its db.insert() call in try/except|catch|rescue and already converts the raise into false. Pinned here so this contract can never silently regress into save() raising.
